development: New AI roles: AI/ML specialists, AI-agent builders and AI governance
definition: Fast-growing roles in AI and machine learning, big data and AI-tool design, with most firms planning to hire AI-skilled staff.
leader_status: Growing globally: WEF 2025 ranks AI/ML specialists among three fastest-growing roles (b6-001; S020); PwC: AI-skill jobs growing 69% faster, 27 countries (b6-006).
analogue_status: Brazil: AI postings 19k to 73k 2021-24 (b6-007). Mexico: AI user and developer roles growing 2025 (b6-008). Poland: AI postings rose 2023-24 (b6-009). Korea, Indonesia: not sourced.
tr_status: exists: AI/ML engineer vacancies listed in Turkish job portals (b6-027; b6-026 secondary); World Bank: AI skills at 0.36% of LinkedIn members, concentrated in few industries (b6-004).
class_branch: 1-2y: C1 (d6 4>=4); 3-5y: C1 (d6 4+1=5 capped; already Certain on sourced d6, not on the +1)
notes: d1 3: Action Plan published (S053) and 2021-25 Strategy AI-expert target (b6-026, secondary); no binding obligation. d2 2: unsourced estimate (no AI-talent call checked; Horizon/TUBITAK not searched for this item). d3 1: AI skills carry a wage premium of 62% (b6-006, snippet), a cost to employers, no saving. d4 3: World Bank puts Turkiye mid-table on AI readiness, digital basics above average (b6-005). d5 2: AI skills 0.36% vs 1.09% Germany, net AI-talent outflow (b6-004). d6 4: AI engineering roles exist in several orgs and sectors (b6-004, b6-027); not scaled. Judgement call on d6 4 vs 3: no Turkish employer-level count seen, only LinkedIn concentration plus job listings; if reviewer sets 3, class would drop to Potential (C4; analogues 3 but d2 2, d3 1). Funded-pilot not applicable (private hiring). WEF figures via search snippets (110% big data, 81% ML in secondary articles, not used); primary weforum.org URLs via search result. Turkiye Today: WEF says 44% of skills change by 2030 in Turkiye (b6-003, headline).

development: Declining clerical and routine cognitive roles
definition: Roles such as cashiers, ticketing clerks, administrative assistants and some accounting tasks projected to shrink as AI automates routine work.
leader_status: USA growing: high-substitution occupations' postings fell 12% vs low, admin support -40% (b6-013); WEF projects clerical roles as steepest decliners (b6-001; S020).
analogue_status: No analogue sourced to the same development. Korea: OECD links older AI to slower permanent-job growth, mainly manufacturing, not clerical (b6-011). Brazil, Mexico, Poland, Indonesia: unsourced.
tr_status: absent: only exposure estimates, no observed clerical decline found. World Bank: 41% of employment in highly exposed occupations, 22% with limited complementarity (b6-004).
class_branch: 1-2y: C1 fail (d1 1, d6 2, funded no) > C2 fail (barrier none, min(d4,d5)=2>1, mean 2.5>=2.0) > C3 fail (d2 2, d3 3 both <4) > C4; 3-5y: no dated obligation, analogues 0 so d6 unchanged, same chain > C4
deciding_condition: Turkish data (TUIK, ISKUR or portal vacancy series) showing an AI-attributable fall in clerical postings or employment, plus employer adoption evidence (would lift d6 to 4+)
notes: d1 1: no obligation tied to clerical automation; no standalone Turkish AI law in force (b6-024, law-firm digest). d2 2: unsourced estimate (reskilling funds such as ISKUR not searched). d3 3: employer substitution incentive shown abroad (b6-013, b6-012: -21% automation-prone writing/coding posts) but no Turkish cost figure. d4 3: workforce digital basics above global average (b6-005). d5 2: persistent skills mismatch, inclusion gaps (b6-004). d6 2: exposure estimate only, not observed decline; Turkish clerical-specific search not done (search budget exhausted), so d6 2 not 1; low confidence. OECD: routine clerical/data-entry prospects declining (b6-010). WEF clerical-decline claim via search snippets of secondary articles plus primary weforum.org URL via search result. Not near-Likely (analogues 0).

definition: Solo and small-firm services that build or run AI workflows for clients, alongside AI-enabled freelancing platforms.
leader_status: USA growing: Upwork AI-skill demand +109% YoY, AI integration +178% (US-sourced demand; b6-014); chatbot-development demand nearly tripled (b6-015).
analogue_status: None sourced. No country-level platform data found for Poland, Brazil, Mexico, Indonesia or South Korea; Payoneer/Fiverr country searches returned nothing usable.
tr_status: absent: Turkish freelance marketplace Bionluk exists (b6-025) but no AI-service seller or micro-agency data found; Turkish freelancer research described as scarce in search results (unsourced figures not used).
class_branch: 1-2y: C1 fail (d1 2, d6 2, funded no) > C2 fail (barrier none, min(d4,d5)=2>1, mean 2.5>=2.0) > C3 fail (d2 2, d3 3 both <4) > C4; 3-5y: no dated obligation, analogues 0 so d6 unchanged, same chain > C4
deciding_condition: Country-level platform or survey data showing Turkish freelancers and micro-agencies selling AI-implementation services beyond isolated cases (d6 4+ would give Certain)
notes: Unsourced estimates: d1 2 (no freelance/platform-work or AI-services rule checked), d2 2 (SME/KOSGEB digital support not searched), d4/d5 partly. d3 3: clients substitute AI for writing/coding freelancers (b6-012 -21% posts; b6-015 -20 to -50% substitutable skills) so cost pressure is moderate and unquantified for Turkiye. d4 3: digital basics above average (b6-005). d5 2: AI skills 0.36% of Turkish LinkedIn members (b6-004). d6 2: platform exists (b6-025), no AI-service evidence after 4 searches EN+TR; low confidence. Sources for A38: no WEF/Upwork/Fiverr country data for Turkiye; WEF Future of Jobs does not cover freelance business models in the snippets seen (S020 is a fastest-growing/declining jobs article, indirect). Upwork 109% is on completed-job earnings with US demand only (b6-014, press release via search result). Fiverr (18,347% AI-agent search surge) and Upwork 34-44% rate premium figures appeared only in secondary blogs and are not used. Platform-claimed Turkish freelancer counts (about 2 million) had no primary source: unsourced estimate, not used. Not near-Likely (analogues 0). Low confidence overall.

development: Algorithmic management and AI in hiring/HR
definition: AI CV screening, interview scoring, scheduling and worker monitoring, classed high-risk under AI Act Annex III.
leader_status: EU regulated: AI Act Annex III employment systems high-risk, obligations now apply 2 Dec 2027 after Omnibus (b6-016; b6-017; b6-019; S042). USA/UK/China adoption status unsourced.
analogue_status: South Korea: 21.7% of top-500 firms use AI in hiring (b6-022). Mexico: firms' stated intent only, not counted (b6-023). Poland, Brazil, Indonesia: unsourced.
tr_status: pilot: MediaMarkt Turkiye runs AI hiring system AI'M Hiring (b6-020, headline); Turkish HR-software vendors exist (b6-021). Broader adoption rates not sourced.
class_branch: 1-2y: C1 fail (d1 3, d6 3, funded no) > C2 fail (barrier none, min(d4,d5)=3>1, mean 3.0>=2.0) > C3 fail (d2 2, d3 3 both <4) > C4; 3-5y: Annex III date 2 Dec 2027 falls before 2028 so no d1 uplift (Annex I embedded 2 Aug 2028 does not cover standalone HR tools); analogues 1<2 so d6 unchanged; same chain > C4
deciding_condition: A sourced finding that the EU AI Act Annex III reach (or KVKK/Turkish AI-law duties) binds a material share of Turkish employers/HR-tech providers (d1>=4 gives Certain)
notes: FLAG d1 borderline 3/4: Annex III obligations (recruitment, promotion, task allocation, worker monitoring) are binding EU law from 2 Dec 2027 (b6-016, b6-017; Omnibus in force 27 Jul 2026), but reach to Turkish actors is only via EU-market providers or EU-used output (b6-018, law-firm digest, snippet); no evidence seen of a material share. If reviewer scores d1 4 (as A39), result is Certain/Certain via C1. Also KVKK Art. 11(1)(g) right to object to purely automated analysis outcomes may already bind Turkish HR use: NOT verified here (search budget exhausted); unsourced, reviewer to check kvkk.gov.tr. Turkish AI bill of 24 Jun 2024 still in committee (b6-024). d2 2: unsourced estimate. d3 3: time-saving claims are vendor-side, no magnitude (stays 3). d4 3, d5 3: unsourced estimates (HR profession exists; TR-language tools exist per b6-020/021). d6 3: single named corporate deployment (b6-020); a claimed 73% Turkish company usage figure appeared in a search summary without traceable source and is not used. tr_funded_pilot no: corporate rollout, no budget evidence seen (a yes would not change class: d2 2, d3 3). Not near-Likely (analogues 1). Confidence low-med. Draft entry had no anchor source: anchor set to Council press release.
